matches.rationale: Findings 1, 2, and 4 all identify fundamental flaws in the statement/proof of Theorem 2.3: Finding 2 explicitly notes that the proof only pins down a single scalar and cannot determine the conjugate vector when the Hodge component has dimension greater than one (h^{n-1-i,i}>1), which is precisely the mechanism described in the ground truth (the construction only works when the Hodge component is 1-dimensional). Findings 1 and 4 attack the same theorem's incorrect claims (mismatched Hodge summands equated, and false equality H_0^{p,q}=H_0^{q,p}) that underlie this same flawed swap-based description of conjugation.
